conventions: Construct chains in this chapter are followed as the ASV writes them. רְקִיעַ עֻזּוֹ is the only chain with a written *of*, which goes to the rectum under rule 19; רֹב גֻּדְלוֹ, תֵקַע שׁוֹפָר, צִלְצְלֵי שָׁמַע and צִלְצְלֵי תְרוּעָה are rendered attributively under rule 28, no relational word is supplied for the rectum, and each noun takes the English word that writes its own lexeme whichever order the ASV puts the two in — so תֵּקַע takes *sound* and שׁוֹפָר the attributive *trumpet*, while צֶלְצְלִים takes *cymbals* and שֶׁמַע the attributive *loud*.

Where one substantive is rendered by two English words, this chapter heads by rule 31's subtraction and not by position, so the direction differs from unit to unit and is not a split: גְּבוּרָה → *mighty acts* heads on *mighty* and מֵן → *stringed instruments* on *stringed*, because *acts* and *instruments* are generics the ASV supplied; תְּרוּעָה → *high sounding* heads on *sounding*, because there the noun's own lexeme is the sounding and *high* is the ASV's specifier. Each unit's note names the competing head under rule 8.
report: Read all six verses end to end against the contract. The ledger is intact (65 units; 64 source and 74 target ids each partitioned once, every head a member of its array) and I found no cross-verse split. Verdict no-change, patches empty.

The three table candidates are context, not splits. הָלַל: every occurrence aligns to its verb and heads on the lexical verb; *Praise ye* in PSA.150.1 and PSA.150.6 folds a supplied subject pronoun into the imperative under rule 17, *Let ... praise* in PSA.150.6 folds the volitive frame of the jussive under the same rule, and the bare *Praise* elsewhere is what the ASV wrote. הוּא: *his* wherever the ASV writes a possessive, *him* wherever it writes the object pronoun — rule 18 read off the English, and each bucket is unanimous. בְּ: the R→Ncmsc bucket holds *in* twice (PSA.150.1, locative, before קֹדֶשׁ and רָקִיעַ) and *with* once (PSA.150.3, instrumental, before תֵּקַע); the relation differs and the morpheme takes the word written for it under rule 11. No בְּ in the chapter fuses with its construct noun under rule 30, because in every case the noun holds an English word of its own.

Checked the construction the keyed table is blind to, since the chapter has exactly one `added` unit. Every other supplied English word is folded into a morpheme that licenses it — *ye* into the imperative (rule 17), the *the* of *the firmament* onto the construct noun (rule 29; no article morpheme stands in that chain), *Let* into the jussive (rule 17), and the generics *acts* and *instruments* into their substantives (rule 31). The one run no morpheme owns, *that hath* in PSA.150.6, is `added` and undivided, headed on *hath* — rule 2's own worked example of this construction (`נָצְרוּ דָעַת` → *him that hath knowledge*). Rule 43 places nothing there: the clause writes no הָיָה, no existential particle, no possessive preposition, no suffix and no noun of possession, and נְשָׁמָה is the thing possessed rather than a בַּעַל-type owner.

Construct chains were checked as a set, since the chapter writes five of them and renders them two ways. רְקִיעַ עֻזּוֹ takes a written *of*, which goes to the rectum under rule 19 with the suffix's *his* under rule 18 and a supplied *the* on the construct under rule 29. רֹב גֻּדְלוֹ, תֵקַע שׁוֹפָר, צִלְצְלֵי שָׁמַע and צִלְצְלֵי תְרוּעָה are rendered attributively and are followed as written under rule 28, with no relational word supplied for the rectum. In each of these the English word goes to the noun whose lexeme it writes, whichever order the ASV puts the two nouns in — hence תֵּקַע → *sound* with שׁוֹפָר → *trumpet*, and צֶלְצְלִים → *cymbals* with שֶׁמַע → *loud*. That is consistent across all five.

The three two-word substantive renderings head in two directions, which is rule 31 rather than an inconsistency: גְּבוּרָה → *mighty acts* and מֵן → *stringed instruments* head on the modifier because *acts* and *instruments* are supplied generics, while תְּרוּעָה → *high sounding* heads on *sounding* because there the noun's own lexeme is the sounding and *high* is the ASV's specifier, exactly as rule 31 heads תַּנִּין → *sea monsters* on *monsters*. Each unit's note already names the competing head under rule 8; I have recorded the direction as a convention so a later reader does not re-open it.

BSB: the single disagreement, the article on נְשָׁמָה in PSA.150.6, is a convention difference and not an error. The ASV writes no *the* and no separate determiner for that morpheme; *everything* is כֹּל's own word, and rule 41 gives a quantifying determiner to a כֹּל standing on the noun before the article, so rule 29's closing sentence marks the article `unrepresented`. BSB attaches the determination to the noun phrase. Nothing to change, and I did not touch an accepted edge to move the aggregate.

No promotions and no amendments. The two judgments this chapter turned on — *that hath* as one `added` unit, and the head of a two-word substantive rendering — are already written into rules 2 and 31 with worked examples of these very shapes, so promoting either would only restate the contract. The eight repeated verse notes the validator flags are all plain restatements of rules 11, 14, 17 and 18 and are not logged as conventions.
